notes.1i: The majority of candidates drew the graph, using the headings from the table to label the axes. The stronger responses used scales of 50.0 to 2cm for the x-axis and 5.0 to 2cm for the y-axis, labelling at least every 2cm. Many candidates also plotted the points precisely with a small cross or dot in a circle and drew a ruled line using a line of best fit.
notes.1ii: Many candidates were able to use their graph to find the time when the rate of mass flow was 20cm3min–1 and showed on the graph how they determined their answer. The most common errors were to give the answer in seconds rather than minutes and not showing on the graph how the answer was determined.
notes.1iii: The majority of candidates correctly stated that the effect of fusicoccin was to increase the rate of mass flow.
notes.1iv: Some candidates correctly referred to fusicoccin binding to receptors of the companion cells, increasing the active transport of hydrogen ions, the role of cotransporters and the transport of sucrose via plasmodesmata.
notes.1v: The majority of candidates were able to suggest ways to change the independent variable in order to have more confidence in their estimate of the concentration of sucrose in U. Many candidates correctly suggested preparing more concentrations of sucrose solution close to the estimate for U with narrower intervals between each concentration. Some candidates gained credit for suggesting that the concentrations of sucrose could be prepared using proportional dilution.
notes.1vi: Many candidates gained credit for stating that plant G was treated with 10cm3 of water instead of fusicoccin solution as it was acting as a control.
notes.2i: Many candidates correctly identified the organ shown in Fig. 2.1 as a stem and gained credit for stating that the vascular bundles were located around the outside, close to the epidermis.
notes.2ii: The majority of candidates gained credit for measuring the length of the vascular bundle using line Z within an acceptable range. Many candidates measured Z in millimetres and showed this figure divided by 20. Most candidates calculated the actual length of the vascular bundle correctly to the appropriate degree of accuracy and used the correct units.
notes.2iii: The majority of candidates correctly stated that the apparatus is a graticule or a stage micrometer.
notes.2c: Many candidates listed at least two observable differences between M1 and Fig. 2.1 such as M1 had fewer vascular bundles than Fig. 2.1 and M1 had scattered vascular tissues while in Fig. 2.1 the vascular tissue was located towards the epidermis.
notes.key_messages: Candidates should use biological terms accurately. For example, in Question 1(a), the secondary structure of antibodies can be described as having beta or β-pleated sheets, not B-pleated sheets and, in Question 1(b)(ii), B-lymphocytes or B cells should be stated, rather than β cells. When quoting extracted data from graphs, candidates are reminded to refer to both axes in their answers. In Question 3(a)(ii), many often omitted the time. In addition, it was better to refer to a specific time from the x-axis rather than to state ‘at the end’.
notes.general_comments: General comments The paper differentiated well. Comments on specific questions The majority of candidates answered correctly, with only the weakest candidates finding it difficult. Questions 2, 4, 6, 16, 19, 23, 30, 34, 37 and 38 Almost all candidates found these questions straightforward and answered correctly. Some candidates found this question difficult. Only the stronger candidates were aware that microtubules carried out all three of the listed functions.
